messages.subject: Nimble webinar Tuesday April 19
messages.body_plain:
Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce,

We'll be holding a webinar on Nimble Tuesday, April 19, with
registration deadline on Friday April 15. Details below.

-Chris

--------------------------------------------------------

ASA Webinar: Programming with Models: An Introduction to NIMBLE, a
BUGS-compatible System for Hierarchical Statistical Modeling Using
MCMC and More

NIMBLE is a new system for programming with hierarchical models in R.
NIMBLE provides analysts with a flexible system for using MCMC,
sequential MC, and other techniques on user-specified models. It
provides developers and methodologists with the ability to write
algorithms in an R-like syntax that can be easily disseminated to
users. C++ versions of models and algorithms are created for speed,
but these are manipulated from R without any need for analysts or
algorithm developers to program in C++. While analysts can use NIMBLE
as a drop-in replacement for WinBUGS or JAGS, NIMBLE provides greatly
enhanced functionality in a number of ways, including customization of
MCMC sampling, user-defined distributions and samplers, and use of
non-MCMC algorithms.

We'll be holding a webinar Tuesday April 19, 3 - 5 pm Eastern. No
previous experience with NIMBLE is required although the webinar will
expect familiarity with the basics of MCMC and with R.

More details are here; the registration deadline is Friday April 15 at
noon Eastern.

http://www.amstat.org/education/weblectures/#PMAINB

messages.subject: version 0.5 of NIMBLE released
messages.body_plain:
Dear nimble-users and nimble-announce,

We're pleased to announce that we've released version 0.5 of NIMBLE at
R-nimble.org.

Version 0.5 is a major release. Highlights include
 - more efficient computations for conjugate sampling,
 - additional automated checking of BUGS syntax to improve NIMBLE’s
warning/error messages,
 - new API functionality to allow the use of syntax such as
model$calculate(), etc. (syntax such as calculate(model) still works),
 - new API functionality for MCMC sampler specification,
 - improvements in speed and memory use in building models, and
 - addition of forwardsolve, backsolve, and solve to the NIMBLE DSL.

More details on the NIMBLE web page and the NEWS file of the package.

Also, we anticipate being on CRAN in upcoming weeks as well as a next
release soon that will include a full suite of sequential Monte Carlo
(i.e., particle filtering) algorithms.

 - Chris Paciorek for the NIMBLE Development Team
